# The difference between cohorts is in the water-rich scans {#sec-water-rich}


::: {.callout-note title="Finding 1"}
In the **fattiest 15%** of samples the three cohorts look the same. In the **wettest 15%** they separate:
NORMAL 0\.81 < BENIGN 0\.96 < CANCER
1\.07 (water peak height). The information is in the water-rich tissue.
:::

Every prepared sample from Nova 250 onwards (intensity-imbalanced patients left out) is shown in @fig-cohort: by Nova number, and ordered by
**water peak height** (the mean of the prepared curve over q = 20-22; preparation sets the fat peak to 1, @sec-preparation). The wettest and
fattiest 15% are marked.

@fig-top15 averages those two bands by cohort. The fattiest 15% overlaps for all three labels (water peak about
0\.12). The wettest 15% pulls apart. Most breast cancers arise in
the glandular tissue [[1]](#references) [[3]](#references), and tumours remodel the fibrous tissue around them [[5]](#references), so a scan
through fat sees little of it.

**Denser is better for us.** Dense breasts hold more glandular, water-rich tissue — exactly where this signal lives. That is where mammography
is weakest (density can hide masses) [[8]](#references) [[9]](#references), so mammography's weakness is our strength: the same tissue that
hurts X-ray contrast is what XRD needs. For **mapping**, keep the wettest points after a whole-breast scan (e.g. the top 15% within
each breast) and compare those (@sec-mapping).

::: {#cell-fig-cohort .cell execution_count=2}

``` {.python .cell-code}
print(f"{len(all_names)} samples from {len(set(map(ne.row_nova, all_names)))} patients, Nova {NOVA_RANGE[0]} onwards")
plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 7
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 3.9))
for ax in axes:
    ax.set_box_aspect(1)
for ax, image_rows in ((axes[0], all_rows), (axes[1], all_rows[all_by_water])):
    covered = np.flatnonzero(np.isfinite(image_rows).all(axis=0))
    columns = slice(covered[0], covered[-1] + 1)
    low, high = np.nanpercentile(image_rows[:, columns], (1, 99))
    left, right = q[columns][[0, -1]]
    ax.imshow(image_rows[:, columns], aspect="auto", cmap=cmap, vmin=low, vmax=high, interpolation="nearest",
              extent=(left, right, len(image_rows), 0))
    ax.set(xlabel="q (nm⁻¹)", xlim=(2, right))
    ax.set_xticks([5, 10, 15, 20])
    ax.axvline(14, color="white", ls="--", lw=0.8)
for (start, stop), colour, text in (((0, all_part), TOP_COLOUR, f"top {PART}%"),
                                    ((len(all_rows) - all_part, len(all_rows)), BOTTOM_COLOUR, f"bottom {PART}%")):
    axes[1].add_patch(plt.Rectangle((2, start), right - 2, stop - start, fill=False, edgecolor=colour, lw=2.5, clip_on=False))
    axes[1].text(right - 0.4, (start + stop) / 2, text, color="white", ha="right", va="center", fontweight="bold")
axes[0].set_yticks([0.5, len(all_names) - 0.5], [f"Nova {ne.row_nova(all_names[0])}", f"Nova {ne.row_nova(all_names[-1])}"])
axes[0].set_ylabel(f"{len(all_names)} samples")
axes[1].set_yticks([])
axes[1].annotate("", xy=(-0.11, 0.9), xytext=(-0.11, 0.1), xycoords="axes fraction",
                  arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color="black", lw=1.2), annotation_clip=False)
axes[1].text(-0.11, 0.07, "Fatty", transform=axes[1].transAxes, ha="center", va="top")
axes[1].text(-0.11, 0.93, "Fibrous/\nGlandular", transform=axes[1].transAxes, ha="center", va="bottom")
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.09, right=0.98, bottom=0.1, top=0.97, wspace=0.4)
plt.show()
plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 10
```

``` {.python .cell-code}
covered = np.flatnonzero(np.isfinite(np.vstack([m for parts in part_means.values() for m, _ in parts.values()])).all(axis=0))
columns = slice(covered[0], covered[-1] + 1)
plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 7
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 3.6), sharey=True)
for ax, part in zip(axes, ("bottom", "top")):
    ax.set_box_aspect(1)
    for label in COHORTS:
        mean, n = part_means[label][part]
        ax.plot(q[columns], mean[columns], color=ne.STATUS_COLOURS[label], lw=1.6,
                label=f"{label}: {n} samples, water peak {part_water[label][part]:.2f}")
    ax.axvline(14, color="black", ls="--", lw=0.8)
    ax.set(title=f"{part.capitalize()} {PART}% ({'fatty' if part == 'bottom' else 'water-rich'})",
           xlabel="q (nm⁻¹)", xlim=(2, 24), ylim=(-0.05, 1.3))
    ax.set_xticks([5, 10, 15, 20])
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper left", fontsize=6)
axes[0].set_ylabel("I(q), prepared (fat peak = 1)")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 10
```
